extracted.intended_audience: regulated entities and practitioners (air carriers/pilots/airport operators, agricultural handlers/committees, exporters/contractors, retailers/companies subject to FTC/SEC rules), and legal/compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and apply substantive regulatory requirements and procedural findings published in a Federal Register rules-and-regulations issue spanning aviation instrument procedures, agricultural marketing orders, export-declaration exemptions, FTC consent orders, and SEC rule actions. Focus is on compliance obligations, definitional cross-references, effective dates, and reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units and measurement conventions for instrument approach procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Bearings, headings, courses and radials are magnetic. Elevations and altitudes are in feet MSL. Ceilings are in feet above airport elevation. Distances are in nautical miles unless otherwise indicated, except visibilities which are in statute miles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to ILS, VOR/DME, radar and other instrument approach procedure text—establishes the units and reference frames used throughout the procedure entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory compliance with prescribed instrument approach procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If an instrument approach procedure of the above type is conducted at the below named airport, it shall be in accordance with the following instrument approach procedure unless an approach is conducted in accordance with a different procedure for such airport authorized by the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Agency. Initial approaches shall be made over specified routes. Minimum altitudes shall correspond with those established for en route operation in the particular area or as set forth below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approaches must follow the published procedure for that airport unless an alternate is specifically authorized by the Administrator; initial routing and minima are binding for operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure contents: transitions, ceiling & visibility minimums, courses/distances, minimum altitudes and condition categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Instrument approach procedure entries include Transition; Ceiling and visibility minimums; Course and distance; Minimum altitude (feet); Condition (aircraft categories: 2-engine or less, 65 knots or less, more than 65 knots, more than 2-engine and >65 knots).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach charts/procedures must present these elements, often in tabular form, specifying minima and conditions by aircraft performance/engine-count categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure-turn and final-approach requirements and missed approach climb
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure turn information (side of course, outbound/inbound headings, altitude within X miles); minimum altitude over facility on final approach; course and distance facility-to-airport; If visual contact not established upon descent to authorized landing minimums or if landing not accomplished within specified distance after passing VOR, climb to specified altitude on a prescribed radial/course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach text specifies exact headings, altitudes and distances for procedure turns and prescribes climb/missed-approach actions tied to loss of visual contact or failure to land within distance limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special authorizations, exceptions, and aircraft-type limitations for minima
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain minima or procedures are 'authorized' except for specified aircraft types or conditions (e.g., '*400-94 authorized, except for 4-engine turbojet aircraft, with operative high-intensity runway lights.' '#100— authorized, except for 4-engine turbojet aircraft, with operative ALS.' Notes allow ATC-authorized DME orbits to eliminate procedure turns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure text will include footnotes and notes specifying when particular minima apply, and exceptions tied to aircraft type (e.g., 4-engine turbojets) and airport lighting/ALS status; operators must observe these exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: ILS-specific approach details (glide slope capture, OM/MM altitudes, missed approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure text gives: minimum altitude at glide slope interception inbound; altitude of glide slope and distance to approach end of runway at OM and MM (e.g., 'at OM, 1560'—6.7 miles; at MM, 217'—0.6 mile'); if visual contact not established upon descent to authorized landing minimums or if landing not accomplished, climb to 1600' on e course of ILS LOC within 20 miles of LOM; '50(h% required when glide slope not utilized.' 'Shawnee Int may be used in lieu of procedure turn when authorized by Palm Beach approach control.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ILS procedures must specify glide-slope interception altitudes/distances, missed-approach climbs, and conditional substitutions of fixes/procedure turns when authorized by ATC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radar instrument approach procedural rules (positive ID, controller authority, missed-approach triggers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Positive identification must be established with the radar controller. From initial contact with radar to final authorized landing minimums, the instructions of the radar controller are mandatory except when (A) visual contact is established on final approach at or before descent to the authorized landing minimums, or (B) at pilot's discretion if it appears desirable to discontinue the approach. A missed approach shall be executed as provided when (A) communication on final approach is lost for more than 5 seconds during a precision approach, or for more than 30 seconds during a surveillance approach; (B) directed by radar controller; (C) visual contact is not established upon descent to authorized landing minimums; or (D) if landing is not accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Radar approaches impose mandatory compliance with ATC vectors and instructions except in narrow circumstances; they impose explicit thresholds for comms loss that require missed approach action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radar vectoring minima, separation and operational cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: All bearings and distances are from the radar antenna site with sector azimuths progressing clockwise. Radar control must provide 3 miles or 1000' vertical separation from specified towers. Note: Minimum radar vectoring altitude (e.g., 1700') may be authorized within specified radius. Cautions include altimeter setting remoted from Memphis Metropolitan Airport; aircraft will not take off under IFR conditions without prior ATC approval; weather service not available at this airport; aircraft will cancel IFR with MEM APC or MEM FSS prior to landing or upon reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Radar approach entries include required vectoring altitudes, separation minima relative to obstacles/towers, and operational cautions related to altimeter settings, IFR takeoff/landing and availability of weather services—operators must follow these operational constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Findings and good-cause basis for immediate effectiveness (agricultural marketing orders)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a marketing committee recommendation is adopted, the Department finds: it is impracticable and contrary to the public interest to give preliminary notice, engage in public rule-making procedure, and postpone the effective date for 30 days because the time between receipt of information and the date the section must be effective is insufficient; a reasonable time is permitted for preparation; committee held an open meeting after due notice; interested persons had opportunity to submit information and views; provisions and effective time are identical with committee recommendation; information disseminated among handlers; compliance will not require special preparation unable to be completed by effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets out the factual/procedural findings that the agency relies on to justify immediate-effect emergency action without full §553 notice-and-comment delay—regulatory drafters and reviewers should document these elements when invoking 'good cause.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment and publication of district-specific handling limits and effective dates
rubrics_metrics.description: The respective quantities of fruit (e.g., Navel oranges, lemons) that may be handled during specified periods are 'hereby fixed' by district (e.g., District 1: 600,000 cartons; District 2: 122,971 cartons; etc.), with an explicit start and end date/time (e.g., beginning at 12:01 a.m. P.s.t., January 9, 1966, and ending at 12:01 a.m. P.s.t., January 16, 1966). 'As used in this section, 'handled,' 'District 1,' etc., have the same meaning as when used in said amended marketing agreement and order.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marketing orders establish numerical handling caps by district and reference back to the definitions in the underlying marketing agreement; handlers must conform to the published district limits during the effective period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of marketable quantity, uniform percentage, and season definitions (celery example)
rubrics_metrics.description: The marketable quantity for the 1965–66 season is established (e.g., 7,762,325 crates). The uniform percentage for the season is determined (e.g., 86.327 percent). During the period January 9, 1966 through July 31, 1966, no handler may handle any harvested celery unless it is within the unused portion of a marketable allotment established for a producer for the entire season. The 1965–66 season is defined (Nov 15, 1965 to July 31, 1966).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order text will set both aggregate marketable quantity and the method (uniform percentage) for allocating handling rights; it also defines the season and constrains handler activity to producers' unused allotments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deduction of previously handled harvested production when computing marketable allotments
rubrics_metrics.description: In computing the total quantity of a producer's harvested celery that may be handled during the remainder of the season, there will be deducted from such producer's marketable allotment such quantity of his harvested celery as was handled during the period November 15–December 15, 1965, and the committee proposed extending the period to such subsequent date as the regulation is issued so that the deduction includes all harvested celery handled up to and including that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocation computations for marketable allotments must subtract previously handled production for a stated historical period (and may extend that historical period to issuance date) so prior handling reduces remaining entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shipper's Export Declaration exemptions for armed-forces shipments (§30.37 and §30.52)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment makes present exemptions and exceptions from the filing of Shipper's Export Declarations for Department of Defense shipments applicable to shipments to armed forces under the jurisdiction of other than the Department of Defense (such as the U.S. Coast Guard). §30.52: 'Shipper’s Export Declarations are not required for the following types of shipments to the United States armed services' including contractor shipments under a Department of Defense or other armed service contract for construction of facilities for use of the United States armed services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exports to armed services and certain contractors are exempt from filing shipper export declarations; the amendment takes effect on date of publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: misuse of comparative price terms (Barney's Order ¶1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the terms 'Reg.', 'formerly', or any other terms of similar import or meaning, to refer to any amount which is in excess of the price at which such merchandise has been sold or offered for sale in good faith by respondents for a reasonably substantial period of time in the recent regular course of their business; or otherwise misrepresenting the price at which such merchandise has been sold or offered for sale by respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative-price labels must refer to bona fide prior selling prices for a reasonably substantial prior period; otherwise their use is deceptive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: misrepresenting 'value' (Barney's Order ¶2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the term 'Val.' or the word 'value', or any other term of similar import or meaning, to refer to any amount which is appreciably in excess of the highest price at which substantial sales of such merchandise have been made in the recent regular course of business in the trade area where such representations are made; or otherwise misrepresenting the price at which such merchandise has been sold in the trade area where such representations are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims of 'value' must be tethered to actual substantial sales in the trade area; overstating 'value' relative to real prior prices is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for representing savings or price comparisons (Barney's Order ¶3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Representing that customers are afforded savings equal to the difference between respondents' stated price and any other price used for comparison is prohibited unless one of several substantiating conditions exists: (a) respondents offered merchandise at the compared price in good faith for a reasonably substantial period in recent regular course; (b) substantial sales are being made in the trade area at the compared price or higher; (c) a substantial number of principal retail outlets in the trade area regularly offer the merchandise for sale at the compared price or higher; or (d) when using value comparison with comparable merchandise, substantial sales of like grade and quality are being made in the trade area at the compared price or higher and it is clearly and conspicuously disclosed that the comparison is with merchandise of like grade and quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Savings and comparative claims must be substantiated by recent, substantial sales data or conspicuous qualifying disclosures; advertisers must be able to satisfy one of the enumerated tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: misrepresenting savings available to purchasers (Barney's Order ¶4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Misrepresenting, in any manner, the savings available to purchasers or prospective purchasers of merchandise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any representation of savings must be accurate and supported; blanket claims of savings without support are prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: misrepresenting quantities available for sale (Barney's Order ¶5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Representing, directly or by implication, that stated quantities of certain merchandise have been purchased or that stated quantities of certain merchandise are available for sale (subject to defense: respondents may establish that such quantities have been purchased or are available as represented).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantity-available claims are actionable if false; defendants have an affirmative defense if they can prove the represented quantities actually existed or were purchased.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: misrepresenting availability and advertised prices (Barney's Order ¶6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Representing, directly or by implication, that merchandise is available for purchase at stated prices or is being or will be sold at such prices (defense: respondents may show that sufficient quantity was available to meet reasonably anticipated demand and that merchandise was sold at or below the advertised price).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertisers must ensure advertised-price availability; short-quantity or bait-and-switch situations are prohibited unless the advertiser can justify sufficiency of stock and sales at or below the advertised price.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent-order reporting requirement (Barney's Order)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents shall, within sixty (60) days after service upon them of this order, file with the Commission a report in writing setting forth in detail the manner and form in which they have complied with this order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent-order respondents must deliver a compliance report to the Commission within the specified timeframe describing remedial steps and policies adopted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition prohibition — Endicott-Johnson divestiture order
rubrics_metrics.description: For a period of 20 years after service of the order, Endicott-Johnson Corp. shall cease and desist from acquiring, directly or indirectly, the whole or any part of the share capital, or assets (other than products sold or purchased in the course of business), of, or any other interest in, any domestic concern engaged principally or as one of its major commodity lines at the time of such acquisition, in any State or DC, in the business of manufacturing or selling shoes or footwear, without the prior approval of the Federal Trade Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-term prohibition on acquisitive expansion in the footwear sector without prior FTC approval—affects corporate M&A and requires pre-clearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divestiture-order reporting requirement (Endicott-Johnson)
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent shall, within sixty (60) days after service upon it of this order, file with the Commission a report in writing setting forth in detail the manner and form in which it has complied with this order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same 60-day compliance-reporting obligation applies to corporate respondents subject to FTC orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission specification of effective dates for adopted rule amendments (SEC example)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is ordered, That the effective date of the amendment (to Rule 16b-3) shall be December 20, 1965.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission may specify the effective date for rule amendments (including retroactive effective dates); regulated parties must note the stated effective date when determining compliance timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of new Regulation 14C (stockholder information statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Securities and Exchange Commission has adopted new Regulation 14C (17 CFR 240.14c–1 to 240.14c–101) relating to the distribution of information pursuant to section 14(c) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adoption of a regulation creates distribution and disclosure obligations for issuers regarding stockholder information statements under section 14(c); details are in the regulation text (not fully reproduced in this chunk).
